priorFindingsVerification.note: Re-read lock.mjs's real withGigLock(statePath, lockKey, fn, opts) signature fresh (lines 187-209) and walked the nested dual-lock design with concrete IDs. REQ-106 now acquires BOTH loan_${lenderId} AND loan_borrower_${borrowerId} for every issuance attempt (behavioral-spec.md:750-756, 767-791), in the order resolveLoanLockAcquisitionOrder returns (line 803), and -- critically -- takes 'a FRESH read of loans.jsonl' and re-evaluates REQ-102(a)-(d) 'while BOTH locks are held ... BEFORE proceeding to REQ-101's own availability recheck' (lines 782-786). Confirmed this fresh read genuinely observes the LATEST committed state, not a stale pre-lock snapshot: ledger.js's appendChild is a plain, synchronous fs.appendFileSync (confirmed via this feature's own repeated citations, e.g. behavioral-spec.md:914-916), so any prior holder's committed write is durably on disk before withGigLock's finally block releases that SAME lock (lock.mjs:203-208) -- and since the fresh read is specified to occur strictly AFTER acquiring the shared loan_borrower_${borrowerId} lock (never before), a second attempt's re-check is structurally guaranteed to see any first attempt's already-appended row. Walked PROP-106n's own concrete scenario (two lenders L1/L2, same borrower B): the two attempts share exactly one lock key (loan_borrower_B); whichever acquires it first proceeds to disburse; the other's re-check, performed only after acquiring that SAME key once released, correctly observes reason:outstanding_loan and refuses. This closes the original cross-lender double-borrowing hole. No remaining gap found in the double-borrowing fix itself -- see FIND-501 below for a SEPARATE, new issue found in this SAME lock-acquisition-order mechanism's own stated JUSTIFICATION (not its correctness).

REQ-102's new condition (d) (behavioral-spec.md:411-426) requires lenderId !== borrowerId, checked FIRST, before (a)/(b)/(c) and before REQ-101's own availability computation ever runs (confirmed also in REQ-106's own Acceptance Criteria, line 1099-1100, and Edge Cases, line 1037-1041: 'rejected by REQ-102(d) BEFORE ANY other step of this critical section runs ... before EITHER lock is acquired'). PROP-102e (verification-architecture.md:110) binds a fixture where the self-loan candidate would otherwise pass every other condition, proving the exclusion is checked independently and first. Genuinely closes the self-loan free-reputation exploit at zero cost.

REQ-106's own text (behavioral-spec.md:855-867) is now unambiguous: issued_ms is a field on the FOLLOW-UP 'active' row ONLY, set to Date.now() at the moment THAT row is appended -- 'it is NEVER the provisional row's own provisioned_ms'. due_ms is always computed from this SAME value (REQ-109, line 1582-1584). PROP-106o (verification-architecture.md:136) binds a fixture where the provisional row is appended at T1 and the active row at a materially later T2, asserting issued_ms===T2 and due_ms computed from T2. The document also honestly discloses the residual reconciled-path timestamp asymmetry as an acknowledged, not-fully-resolved limitation (lines 868-881) rather than papering over it. No remaining gap found.

evidence.description: computeColdStartRepaymentRate/evaluateColdStartKillSwitch -- the ONLY automated default-risk monitoring/pause mechanism this feature builds -- is scoped exclusively to successfulOnTimeRepayments===0 loans, structurally excluding any default among established borrowers holding the largest ($0.04-$5.00) loans from ever influencing the pause decision

The document's own header still declares 'revision: iteration 3' and its Changelog tables stop at 'iteration 2 -> iteration 3', even though the body text demonstrably incorporates iteration 3/4/5 resolutions (FIND-201..403) throughout -- RESOLUTION-NOTES.md exist on disk for iterations 3-5 but are never referenced the way iteration-1/2's are

withGigLock/acquire() is a single, non-blocking, fail-fast primitive with no retry/wait loop -- confirmed fresh this session -- meaning REQ-106's own 'textbook total-lock-ordering deadlock-avoidance' justification (behavioral-spec.md:793-802) describes a hold-and-wait scenario that cannot occur against this mechanism, independent of key-acquisition order

PROP-106m tests only that resolveLoanLockAcquisitionOrder returns a correctly-sorted key pair -- no proof obligation anywhere in the 149-item table attempts to construct, exercise, or measure an actual deadlock, because none is constructible against this lock mechanism
